title: The Clock of the Lower Danube
premise: In the waning years of a contested borderland along the Lower Danube, Noor Blackwood, a mapmaker's apprentice of no fixed nation, completes the atlas his dying master smuggled out at terrible cost — an atlas that records villages the coming census intends to erase from existence. When a census taker named Aurel arrives with orders to certify the maps as blank, Noor hides him instead of turning him in, and the two men become unlikely conspirators racing the victors' historians to get the true record notarized and carried downriver. Betrayed by the guild that trained Noor and hunted by the very officials who killed his master, they deliver the atlas to a river archive on the eve of its burning, trading Noor's name, citizenship, and future for the truth's survival. The book ends with the atlas entered into the record under both their names — an inheritance neither was born to, shared by choice.
about_author: Ivo Brightwater is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed border maps before turning to fiction. He writes from a houseboat on a slow European river, where he claims the water keeps better records than any government.

chapters.title: The Weight of Rivers
chapters.summary: Noor Blackwood's POV. In the dead master's flooded workshop, Noor finishes the final plates of the forbidden atlas while guild inspectors circle closer, measuring everything he owns by what can be carried in one satchel. He discovers his master's hidden letter naming him heir — and naming the archive downriver where the atlas must go. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; the loneliness of inheriting a dangerous truth alone.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Noor and Aurel, the census taker sent to certify the district as empty. During his inspection, Aurel asks about a village Noor knows exists, then quietly pockets a page of evidence instead of reporting it. Caught between duty and conscience, Aurel returns after hours and asks Noor for sanctuary. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two men on opposite sides of the same ledger; the first crack in Aurel's obedience.

chapters.title: The Burning Season
chapters.summary: Aurel's POV, with Noor present. The guild betrays them, selling the atlas's location to the victors' commission; the workshop burns and their found family of riverfolk scatters or dies covering the escape. Fleeing by barge through fog and patrol boats, Noor and Aurel confess what they've each lost for love of the work — and admit what they've found in each other. Emotional beat: climax of pursuit and devotion; love declared with the archive smoke rising behind them.

chapters.title: Entered Into Record
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the river archive, minutes ahead of the official purge, Noor and Aurel force a dying notary to witness the atlas into the permanent record under both their names — Noor surrendering his claim to citizenship, Aurel his career and name. They walk away stateless but unerasable, the truth now belonging to anyone who reads. Emotional beat: quiet triumph and costly peace; inheritance redefined as something chosen, not given.
